items.name: GJ 229 b

Rejected because.value: LIKELY ACTIVITY. A line-by-line reanalysis of the HARPS RVs finds the ~526 d signal vanishes once stellar activity (Prot 28.9 d) is modelled, and excludes the Tuomi et al. 2014 amplitude at 95% and Feng et al. 2022's at 92% (Deslieres et al. 2025, AJ 169, 182). Not formally refuted.
Rejected because.source: Deslieres, Cadieux, Doyon et al. 2025, AJ 169, 182, 'The Gl 229 System Revisited with the Line-by-line Framework: Planetary Signals Now Appear as Stellar Activity Ghosts', abstract, Sect. 3-5

Confidence tier.source: Rejected candidates tab: every one of its 87 rows uses 'unlikely'

items.reason: Deslieres et al. 2025 (AJ 169, 182) attribute the GJ 229 b signal to systematics and stellar activity ('most probably of stellar origin'); the discovery group has since said the inner companions 'cannot be confirmed' (Feng et al. 2025, MNRAS 539, 3180).
items.notes: Is this a refutation? No, not formally. Deslieres et al. conclude the signals 'are most probably of stellar origin' and 'vanish when stellar activity is taken into account' (GP on the LBL dLW indicator, Prot = 28.9 +/- 1.6 d; BIC: no planet 867, planet b 906, planet c 887). The '3 sigma' in the brief is their HZ upper limit (9.1 M_E, ~15 M_E near Prot), not a 3-sigma rejection of the planets. Amplitude tests: Tuomi et al. 2014's b excluded at 95%, Feng et al. 2022's b at 92%; for c they 'cannot reject the semiamplitude of F. Feng et al. (2022)'. So the fair label is 'not confirmed, likely activity' (LIKELY ACTIVITY), matching the tab's GJ 754 b / GJ 846 b entries, not REFUTED. Later papers: none found that re-claims the planets. Feng, Xiao, Jones et al. 2025 (MNRAS 539, 3180, Sect. 4.3), from the discovery group, say 'the existence of inner companions cannot be confirmed by the current astrometric and RV data'. Against: Mignon et al. 2024 (A&A 689, A32; arXiv:2502.06513, Table 4 'previously discovered and recovered') recover 121.49 d and 528.17 d signals at FAP < 1e-3 in HARPS with only sinusoid activity correction, and Mignon et al. 2025 (A&A 700, A146; arXiv:2502.06553, Table 5) still count both in their occurrence statistics, while noting GJ 229 shows 'RV signals at varying periods across different seasons'. Both predate or ignore Deslieres and do not model activity with a GP. NASA pscomppars still lists GJ 229 b and GJ 229 A c (2026-09-27). WebFetch of the IOP page supplied the quotes; the paper has no arXiv version that I could find. Sheet period 526.115 d differs from NASA pscomppars 579.47 d (Feng 2022); moot once rejected.

items.reason: The discoverers call their own 2014 interpretation 'invalid' (Tuomi et al. 2019, App. A.43), and an independent refereed reanalysis fails to confirm GJ 682 c (Feng et al. 2020, ApJS 246, 11).
items.notes: Tuomi 2019 hedges: 'should it turn out that some of the HARPS data are indeed biased, this interpretation would require reassessment' (four of nine new HARPS RVs drive the disagreement). Mignon et al. 2024 (A&A 689, A32) did not recover the GJ 682 planets but blame too few HARPS nights (Sect. 7.4.1), which is neutral. NASA still lists both (2026-09-27).

items.name: Kapteyn c

Rejected because.value: ROTATION. A joint RV + H-alpha Gaussian-process model gives Prot = 125 d, next to the 121.5 d period; adding a planet does not help and no residual signal remains, so 'both previously reported "planets" are artifacts of the star's rotation and activity' (Bortle et al. 2021, AJ 161, 230).
Rejected because.source: Bortle et al. 2021, AJ 161, 230, abstract, Sect. III.2 and IV

Confidence tier.source: Rejected candidates tab: every one of its 87 rows uses 'unlikely'

items.reason: Bortle et al. 2021 (AJ 161, 230) conclude 'Kapteyn's star does not host any exoplanets'; the 121.5 d signal sits on the 125 d rotation period and is absent from the GP residuals (FAP > 10% everywhere).
items.notes: Kapteyn b is already on Rejected (see incidental_finds), so the same verdict for c keeps the system consistent. Only the discoverers' rebuttal (Anglada-Escude et al. 2015, arXiv:1506.09072) predates Bortle; nothing later re-claims c. Mignon et al. 2024 (A&A 689, A32; arXiv:2502.06513, Table 8) do fit the 228 HARPS RVs of GJ 191 with a constant, but their Sect. 7.4.1 puts the missed GJ 191 planets down to using HARPS alone, so I left that out of the verdict (the existing Kapteyn b entry cites it as support). NASA pscomppars still lists Kapteyn c (2026-09-27).

incidental_finds: Kapteyn b is already on Rejected candidates (tier 'unlikely') and not on the Planets tab, which is right. Its 'Rejected because' text is a copy of the long TIER note, has no leading verdict tag, and ends with a note to the writer ('the writer may prefer to treat it as refuted'). Suggest: 'ROTATION. 48.6 d is Prot/3 (Robertson et al. 2015, ApJL 805, L22) and a joint RV + H-alpha GP (Prot 125 d) finds no planet: both reported planets are rotation and activity artifacts (Bortle et al. 2021, AJ 161, 230).' Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.02709

GJ 680 Systems row: 'Stellar Class' K5 (and 'Planet-host class' K5, sort key 55) looks wrong. SIMBAD gives CD-48 11837 = GJ 680 = HIP 86057 as M1.5V (Gray et al. 2006, 2006AJ....132..161G), Philipot et al. 2023 Table 7 gives M3V, and Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot Teff is 3235 K. 'Host mass' is blank: Philipot et al. 2023 Table 7 gives 0.47 +/- 0.01 Msun (Kervella et al. 2022); 'Effective temp' is blank: Gaia DR3 3235 K. With Teff filled, the 'HZ distance' cell ('Teff outside 2600-7200 K') would need recomputing. Sources: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-tap/sync , https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.05417 , https://gea.esac.esa.int/tap-server/tap/sync

Feng et al. 2025 (MNRAS 539, 3180; arXiv:2412.14542), 'Lessons learned from the detection of wide companions', is the Feng group's own correction of its 2022 catalogue: it also reclassifies HD 211847 B and HD 111031 B as low-mass stars (Sect. 4.4, Table 4), and says F22 made HD 62364 look like it had two companions through a Bayes-factor error (Sect. 4.3). Anyone checking other Feng et al. 2022 planets on the sheet should read it.
